sonnet.q1: Captured amount minus the total of pending and succeeded refunds on that payment (failed refunds don't count). The new amount plus that total must not exceed the captured amount.
sonnet.q2: The server retries with the same idempotency key, up to 3 more times (max 4 calls total, 10-second timeout each). If all fail, the refund stays pending and the reconciliation job picks it up.
sonnet.q3: The refund is marked failed, with no retry. The provider's message is saved and shown to the admin, and an audit entry is written for the status change.
sonnet.q4: A refund.succeeded event (webhook, or the reconciliation job applying the same result) that moves a pending refund to succeeded, and only if the refund has no 'email sent' mark. The mark is set when the email is sent.
sonnet.q5: The sum of only the succeeded refunds on the payment: none gives no change, less than captured gives Partially refunded, equal to captured gives Refunded. It is recalculated when step 5 (or step 7) sets a refund to succeeded. Pending and failed refunds never change it. If the update fails, it is recalculated the next time a refund on that payment changes.
sonnet.q6: In one database transaction, the server locks the payment row, so two refunds on the same payment wait for each other. Each then adds the pending and succeeded refunds plus its new amount and rejects the request if the total exceeds the captured amount.
sonnet.q7: The server generates a new idempotency key in step 3 when it creates the pending refund. It is saved on the refund row in our database, so every retry in step 4 reuses it.
sonnet.q8: The signature is checked first. The refund is found by the provider's refund ID. If it is already succeeded or failed, the event is ignored. Only a pending refund gets its status set (with an audit entry). The email is sent only if the 'email sent' mark is unset, and the mark is set when sending. Matching a webhook that arrives before the provider refund ID is saved is not yet decided.
sonnet.q9: It stays pending. The provider may have created the refund anyway, and the same key prevents a second one. The reconciliation job in step 7 checks it later.
sonnet.q10: The reconciliation job (step 7) does this. It runs on a schedule, but how often is NOT STATED, beyond needing to be often enough that no refund stays pending over 24 hours. It finds refunds pending more than 24 hours and asks the provider for the current status. It applies the same result as a webhook (succeeded or failed sets the status, writes an audit entry, and for succeeded sends the email once) and then runs step 6. If the provider cannot answer, the refund stays pending and the job retries on its next run.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED. The document only says that a refund left pending after all retries fail is shown as pending, and that a 4xx failure shows the provider's message. It does not say what the admin sees right after a normal submission.
